target: Next hourly median systematics-corrected stellar flux
independent_unit: Star; repeated hourly bins are dependent
timing_contract: Predict next disjoint hourly bin using preceding observed hourly medians only. The released light curve was author-corrected using full-sector information; this is a retrospective product-space forecast, not a raw real-time pipeline.
calibration: Causal observed flux history within each star; no fitted header period or future light curve values.
scope_limits: Eight selected stars in one TESS sector; no new planet, stellar period or universal rotation law. Missing per-cadence quality/error columns limit robustness.
split: Two stars with smallest seeded SHA256 identifiers held; leave-one-star-out development folds
question: Does a damped local dynamical model transfer between stars better than persistence?
exposure: Source-aware public data. Limited schema/header and first-row previews recorded before task freeze; any inspected examples remain explicitly exposed. Confirmation performance withheld until selection and stopping freeze.
uncertainty_policy: Report per-group errors and worst-group error; no independent-row confidence intervals; one-event and finite catalogs are conditional diagnostics.
selection: Lowest development mean-group MAE, simpler model on relative1% tie. Exact mathematical algorithm baselines do not claim novel accuracy. Retain every attempt and compare named strong controls.
stopping: At least5distinct scientific attempts; continue while a justified distinct mechanism yields prediction/robustness/interpretation gain; stop after2consecutive substantive no-gain attempts after minimum5.
